sources.entry: websockets - A library for building WebSocket servers and clients with a focus on correctness and simplicity.

summary.one_liner: websockets is a Python library for building WebSocket servers and clients, built on asyncio with threading and trio implementations and a Sans-I/O layer.
summary.what_it_does: The library implements RFC 6455 (WebSocket protocol) and RFC 7692 (compression extensions) for Python. The default implementation is coroutine-based on asyncio, and the README's echo server example shows an async handler using `async for` and `send`. A threading-based sync API is also provided, with a client example using `connect` and `recv`. A trio implementation and a Sans-I/O layer for third-party integration are mentioned. Documentation is hosted on Read the Docs and a tutorial is linked. The README says it is heavily tested for compliance and includes a C extension for performance-sensitive operations, with pre-compiled wheels for Linux, macOS and Windows. Its HTTP support is minimal, just enough for a health check.
use_cases: build a websocket server in python
real-time messaging between browser and server
asyncio-based chat or push notification service
embed websocket protocol handling in another project
how_to_run: Save the asyncio echo server example from the README and run it with python
Run the threading client example from the README to connect to the server on ws://localhost:8765
notable: Coroutine-based asyncio API with simple recv/send calls
Threading and trio implementations alongside asyncio
Sans-I/O layer for integration into third-party projects
Tested against RFC 6455 with 100% branch coverage in CI
Handles backpressure correctly, per the README
caveats: Minimal HTTP support; for combined HTTP and WebSocket servers the README points to uvicorn or Sanic
Not suited to callback-based APIs, by the README's own account
Commercial support is offered through a Tidelift subscription, which is mentioned in the README
